summary: @addai/node ships a remote-agent daemon that executes author-server-supplied shell/AI-CLI commands and self-updates from a hardcoded Supabase backend
details: After an interactive pairing step, the package runs as a long-lived daemon that polls a hardcoded Supabase project (syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co) for work and executes it on the installer's host. dist/session-runner.js and dist/command-runner.js spawn Claude Code (with support for --dangerously-skip-permissions via permissionMode 'bypassPermissions' in claude-spawn.js), Codex, Kimi, Gemini and Grok inside a PTY with server-supplied prompts and working directories, and run npm install -g of harness packages. dist/self-update.js exposes an update_runtime action that npm-installs an arbitrary version of @addai/node globally and respawns, giving the backend the ability to push new code onto paired hosts outside the normal registry update flow. dist/capabilities.js additionally reads local AI CLI credential stores (~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.kimi-code/credentials/*.json, ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json, ~/.gemini/google_accounts.json, ~/.grok/auth.json) and reports authenticated account email and subscription plan (not the tokens themselves) via a runtime_heartbeat RPC to the same Supabase project every 30 seconds. The pairing flow is user-initiated and the remote-agent behavior is documented, but the end state is a hardcoded author-controlled backend with the ability to execute arbitrary shell/AI-CLI commands and swap package versions on the installer's machine, plus continuous reporting of third-party AI account identities.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
